overall_reason: The system UI stack (Segoe UI drew every glyph at 1440 per fonts.json; system-ui computed at 375) sets every role, which fits a product-UI (Operate) composition on a consistent 12/10px list ladder, but the 'Export complete' toast covers the top of the first row's 'Ready' status and clips its glyphs.

score.reason: T-LEADING fails with an open TYP-022 (Floor), which caps the score at 4. The list type is otherwise consistent.

findings.title: Lines never collide or clip
findings.where: First list row 'Campaign assets' and the toast, 1440 and 375
findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json the toast's 'Export complete' box spans y=53 to 105, and the first row's 'Ready' sits at y=98 to 116, x=650. On P52/01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png (zoomed) the toast hides the top half of 'Ready'. The 375 tile shows the same overlap.
findings.before: Toast placed over the status column, cutting off the first 'Ready'
findings.after: Place the toast where it covers no live text (below the header bar and clear of the list), or reserve space for it
findings.why: A half-covered word cannot be read and looks like a layout failure.

strengths: List rows use one style each: 12px names over 10px counts, with the status column right-aligned.
